newsitem.title: UK: Gold firm after spike in silver but seen fragile.
newsitem.headline: Gold firm after spike in silver but seen fragile.

text.p: Bullion hovered just above $347.00 an ounce on Monday as silver recouped some of last week's losses, but dealers said the downside risk remained.

"It's a question of waiting for a move. I would have thought that most people think the market will try lower rather than higher, although the more time elapses the less easy it is to pick which way it's going," said one London dealer.
Gold fixed a touch higher at $347.85 from Friday's $347.40.
Support held well at $347.00 while prices clung to a narrow range, but dealers said support might falter unless the market gathered upside momentum soon.
"I get the impression that the market is basically static and in a plateau phase," said the dealer.

Precious metals found some respite from selling pressure after Friday's stronger close in COMEX futures, but some dealers were still wary of fresh fund selling when New York futures trade opened, particularly in silver.
Charts indicators suggested silver was due for a correction, although downside pressure was seen intact in the medium term.
Analysts said a break above $4.80 might spark short covering towards $4.90 and possibly $5.00, while critical support was pegged at $4.55/$4.60.
Silver was indicated higher but off peaks at $4.75/$4.77 per ounce against Friday's close of $4.72/$4.74.
Palladium spiked higher, fuelled by fresh signs that Russian PGM shipments to Japan will be further delayed.

Russia's trade representative in Japan said there would be no shipments in April and that May shipments were in doubt. Almaz, Russia's platinum group metal export agency, had not yet received its export licence.
"On Friday, late in the afternoon there was quite a lot of borrowing from the Swiss banks. Liquidity got tight and the metal followed it up," said one dealer.
Dealings were quiet on Monday with prices indicated at $147.50/$148.50, up 75 cents from Friday's close.
"Platinum is going to go up when palladium goes up, but it will go up a bit slower. There isn't a liquidity problem with platinum," said the dealer.
